A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same reasoning-pattern study, retaining the central framework, RLVR convergence results, and larger-model comparisons. Both versions’ main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reasoning-pattern distributions and success-rate measurements across mathematical tasks, plus numerical case studies and Long Arithmetic training dynamics (Figures 2, 4–6).

after.justification: V2 reports original RLVR–RLIF training comparisons, token-rank measurements, reasoning-pattern trajectories, and numerical simulations (Figures 1–3 and Table 1), alongside retained larger-model results.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a new optimizer or model architecture, and v2 does not establish a modification to RLVR itself. RLIF is added as an existing approach to compare and analyze; changes to the mathematical framework and analysis protocols are distinct from a proposed algorithm change.

E1.justification: V2 adds GSM8K evaluation for token-level analysis and removes the Easy Countdown and Long Arithmetic experiments. Their prompts remain in Appendix D, but no corresponding experiments are reported. MATH-derived tasks, AMC23, AIME24, and OlympiadBench remain represented.

E2.justification: V2 adds RLIF as a direct comparator to RLVR in matched Qwen2.5-3B training and token-level comparisons. The Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct versus SimpleRL-Zoo and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct versus QwQ-32B comparisons are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E3.justification: V2 introduces matched 3B-model training on MATH, evaluation every 20 steps, and token-rank comparisons using fixed base-model responses to 400 questions each from GSM8K and MATH and the full AIME24 dataset. Pattern dynamics use 1,024 responses per question. The stated pattern classifier changes from DeepSeek-V3 to GPT-4o; this does not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds longitudinal Number Theory and Geometry pattern analyses, token-level diagnostics, and RLIF simulations examining initial improvement, eventual degradation, and dependence on the number of patterns. V1’s Long Arithmetic case study varying SFT initialization disappears. The two RLVR toy convergence cases are retained and redrawn.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly reports three training curves per reward method using different random seeds (Appendix B.1 and Figure 1). V1 reports extensive response sampling but no corresponding training-seed protocol. This introduces seed-replication reporting, without establishing an increase in runs for an existing experiment; confidence intervals and significance tests remain absent.

E6.justification: V2 adds training trajectories showing stable RLVR gains versus RLIF improvement followed by degradation, token-rank results, and RLIF simulation outcomes. For example, Table 1 reports MATH rank-change ratios at step 100 of 6.6% for RLVR and 8.8% for RLIF. Easy Countdown and Long Arithmetic results are removed. Retained 7B and 32B plots are reorganized, not evidence of new performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 generalizes the optimal-policy statement to both reward types, adds Assumption 5.5 and Theorem 5.6 concerning RLIF’s initial accuracy derivative and asymptotic selection of the least accurate pattern, and supplies a new Appendix C.5 proof. V1’s SFT convergence theorem and proof are removed. The two RLVR convergence theorems remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: V1 centers on RLVR selecting effective existing patterns and SFT improving initialization. V2 broadens the main contribution to RL training dynamics, claims that sparse token changes reshape pattern distributions, and contrasts RLVR with RLIF’s initial gains and possible eventual degradation. The SFT acceleration contribution is dropped.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation of RLIF failure through confidence rewards that cannot distinguish correctness, and interprets sparse token-rank changes as driving pattern redistribution. It adds qualifications concerning base-model assumptions while retaining limitations about pattern interpretability and simplified theory. V1’s substantive interpretation of SFT as improving RLVR initialization is removed.

D1.justification: The revised Appendix B documents the verl MATH example configuration, the library procedure for querying token probabilities and ranks, GPT-4o temperature zero, and more explicit answer-removal instructions for continuation-based accuracy analysis. Earlier SFT dataset sizes and training-step details for the removed tasks disappear. Most full prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The broad RLHF-centered review is replaced by positioning against research on entropy, internal rewards, sparse token updates, and amplification of pretrained behavior. Newly discussed works include Agarwal et al., Cui et al., Huan et al., and Zhao et al. V1’s claim to take the first reasoning-pattern perspective is replaced by a more comparative training-dynamics positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, preliminaries, and conclusions are extensively rewritten. Section 4 becomes a progression from training overview to pattern-level and token-level analysis; case studies receive a separate section, and experimental setup is reorganized in Appendix B. This substantially changes the narrative beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: V1’s pipeline and framework overview figures are removed. V2 adds training-dynamics plots and a token-rank table, and combines redrawn RLVR cases with new RLIF simulations. Earlier Number Theory and Geometry panels move into a combined appendix figure with the other 7B results; the 32B figure is retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through matched RLVR–RLIF trajectories, three seeded runs, and clearer analysis instructions. However, its new central claims raise unresolved reliability concerns: token-rank stability alone does not establish the claimed causal mechanism, and Appendix C.5 asserts probability-one initial improvement without controlling empirical-to-integral approximation error relative to the vanishing positive bias. These concerns, alongside replacement of the SFT analysis, prevent a confident net quality judgment.
